standard_text: Does the scale consist of effect indicators (a reflective model) so that a factor or IRT/Rasch model is appropriate?

Was the sample size adequate? CTT factor analysis: Very good = >=7x items and >=100; Adequate = >=5x items and >=100 or >=7x items but <100; Doubtful = >=5x items but <100; Inadequate = <5x items. IRT/Rasch: see references/cosmin.md.
Was the analysis appropriate and model fit reported (CFA or Rasch/IRT with fit statistics = Very good; EFA only = Adequate; no fit statistics = Doubtful; no factor/IRT analysis = Inadequate)?
Were there any other important flaws in the design or statistical methods?
Was an internal consistency statistic calculated for each unidimensional scale or subscale separately?
Was Cronbach's alpha or omega (continuous items) / KR-20 (dichotomous) / an IRT reliability or SE estimate calculated?
Were there any other important flaws?
Were patients stable in the interim period on the construct being measured?
Was the time interval between the two measurements appropriate?
Were the test conditions similar for both measurements (administration mode; environment; instructions)?
Was an ICC (continuous; model/formula stated = Very good, not stated = Adequate; Pearson/Spearman without evidence of no systematic change = Doubtful) or (weighted) kappa (categorical) calculated?
